title: Logspace Simulation Preserves Output Probabilities
statement: Let a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages have a finite control-state set with decidable equality, and suppose every oracle language belongs to $\text{LOGSPACE}$. For natural numbers $C_0,c_0$, assume that for every input $x$ some length $N$ makes the program halt on every choice string of length $N$, with each pre-final configuration satisfying its validity conditions and having every register value at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$. Then there are a natural number $c$ and a finite-state nondeterministic machine that uses at most $c$ times logarithmic space on every input, and such that for every $x,N$ for which the stated halting and configuration conditions hold, the machine halts within some time $T$ and, for each bit $b$, the probability that it outputs the one-bit string $[b]$ after $T$ steps equals the probability that the register program answers $b$ after $N$ choices.
hypotheses_covered: The program has $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages
The finite control-state set has decidable equality
Every oracle language is in LOGSPACE
For each input, some length $N$ makes every choice string of that length halt
Every pre-final run configuration satisfies the program's validity conditions
Every register value is at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$
The simulated-machine conclusion applies to every $x,N$ satisfying those halting and configuration conditions
